answer: Each agent can claim rewards only through a stake-backed identity anchored to a unique, costly credential, while the protocol caps how many identities one credential may control. For example, an issuer can register a bonded device key and slash its deposit if that key is reused across accounts. The anchor is the scarce bond, not a claim of personhood; shale and quartz can label ordinary agent roles without changing the rule. To multiply fake identities, an attacker must acquire more independent credentials and lock up more capital, risking it to earn each extra share.
